The test duct had a diameter of 16 mm and a length-to-diameter ratio of 20.
The duct was oriented eccentrically with an eccentricity of 0.2.
The Reynolds number was below 100,000 and the rotation number was below 0.2.
Cooling air ejection was simulated using 32 holes, 2 mm in diameter, spaced at s/d = 2 along the duct.
Flow visualization using a co-rotating camera and laser light sheet showed that pressure side ejection strengthened the secondary vortices, while suction side ejection weakened them.
Velocity measurements revealed a strongly kidney-shaped velocity distribution with pressure side ejection, indicating enhanced secondary vortices.
Suction side ejection resulted in smoother velocity profiles with weaker vortex motion.
Wall temperature distributions showed larger differences around the duct circumference with pressure side ejection due to the stronger secondary vortices.
The effect of cooling air ejection was found to be more dominant than the effect of rotation on the flow and heat transfer behavior.
The Laser-2-Focus (L2F) anemometry technique was used for the non-intrusive velocity and turbulence measurements.
The velocity measurement uncertainty ranged from ±0.5% in the core flow to ±3.0% near the wall, while the angle determination uncertainty was between ±0.2° and ±1.0°.
Numerical flow analysis was used to provide additional insights into the flow physics, including the dominant effect of bleeding on the displacement of the flow core.
